items.title: HSY Q3 deep dive: innovation pipeline and productivity efforts shape outlook amid muted volume trends
items.summary: Chocolate company Hershey (NYSE:HSY) reported Q3 2026 results beating Wall Street’s revenue expectations, with sales up 3% year on year to $3.28 billion. Its non-GAAP profit of $2.64 per share was 25.1% above analysts’ consensus estimates.

items.title: In Biden’s First Halloween In Office, A 100-Piece Bag Of Candy Cost $9.91, A Study Found. This Year It’s $16.96, And Government Data Shows Candy Prices Rose 7.7% In A Year, More Than Double Overall Inflation
items.summary: Halloween candy prices have climbed far faster than anything else in your shopping cart, and Hershey's latest earnings report reveals exactly why candy makers have little reason to stop raising prices anytime soon.

items.title: Hershey (HSY) stock trades up, here is why
items.summary: Shares of chocolate company Hershey (NYSE:HSY) jumped 2.8% in the afternoon session after the company reported third-quarter 2026 financial results with higher consolidated net sales and adjusted diluted earnings per share, and management raised its full-year adjusted earnings growth outlook. Consolidated net sales reached $3.275 billion, an increase of 3.0% for the third quarter of 2026. Adjusted diluted earnings per share was $2.64, an increase of 103.1%.

items.title: Hershey (HSY) Stock Rises As Q3 Earnings Spotlight Margin Strength
items.summary: Hershey stock snapped higher, climbing 3.3% to US$165.61 by Friday’s close, even though the past week had been tough with the share price down over 2%. Traders latched onto one thing in the fresh Q3 2026 release: profit power. Basic earnings per share came in at US$2.89 on revenue of US$3.28b, pointing to a quarter where the real story was margin strength, not just sales volume. items.title: Hershey (HSY) Stock Gets Fair Value Trim As Analysts Question Earnings Durability
items.summary: Hershey’s modeled fair value has been trimmed from about US$201.05 to about US$193.48, a cut of roughly 3.8% that brings the price target closer to where more cautious estimates sit. That shift lines up with recent Street research, where most firms are fine tuning Hershey targets rather than changing their broader view, as they weigh questions about earnings dependability and category growth.
